text: {"score":2,"justification":"The numeric facts mostly match the card (34.1% of 633, expected 4.0%, z 4.95, 43% low-complexity share, 30 records, 0 of 11 documented 99215 below billed). But the headline and leaning are incoherent: the headline reports 0 of 11 documented 99215 claims below billed, which weakens the upcoding concern. The summary still says 'consistent with upcoding' without reconciling this. All 11 documented 99215 claims were supported, and 4 are shown on the card as high MDM, yet the summary never presents this as a counterpoint. The 'against 17% for comparison providers' figure is the card's all_provider_rate of 0.174, so it is grounded. The cited examples C0095731 and C0095830 are below-billed documented claims for 99213 and 99214, not 99215, so they don't support the 99215 pattern the rationale argues. They are only loosely relevant. Next steps are partly sensible, but they request audit trails and charts for a mix of claims and don't ask for documentation of the 99215 claims that were actually documented or the low-complexity examples beyond one. 'Problems 37%' and 'late 13%' could not be matched by the script, and they cannot be verified on the card. The summary says nothing about 190 excess claims or the 5+ condition rows. It does flag caution ('not a finding').","problems":["Headline reports 0% below billed for documented 99215, which cuts against the upcoding leaning, and the tension is never explained","Examples C0095731 (99213) and C0095830 (99214) are not 99215 claims and do not support the 99215 upcoding argument","Note-check percentages (37% problems, 13% late, etc.) are not on the evidence card and cannot be verified; the script flagged 10 and 37","Next steps request audit trails for claims unrelated to the main pattern; only one of three low-complexity 99215 claims is included in chart requests","Does not note that the documented 99215 claims were all supported at high MDM, which is a counter-signal","Excess 99215 claims (190.5) and the complexity gradient are omitted, leaving the billed vs complexity comparison thin"]}
